Line of Business:
Risk Management Job Description:
We are seeking a highly analytical and strategic Credit Card Collections Strategy Manager to drive performance optimization across the collections lifecycle. This role will leverage advanced data analytics and segmentation techniques to design, test, and optimize collections strategies that improve customer outcomes while ensuring compliance with regulatory standards.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in credit card collections, strong analytical capabilities, and a knowledge-seeking, hypothesis-driven mindset to continuously refine strategies.

Key Responsibilities
-  Develop and execute collections strategies across delinquency stages (early- to late-stage), with focus on improving cure rates, roll rates, and customer engagement
-  Leverage data analytics and segmentation to design targeted treatment strategies (SMS, digital, call, legal routing)
-  Drive test-and-learn frameworks, including control/treatment design, performance measurement, and statistical validation
- Identify customer segments using behavioral, risk, and engagement data to optimize outreach and recovery strategies
-  Partner with cross-functional teams (Legal, Compliance, Operations, Digital Vendors) to implement compliant and scalable strategies
-  Monitor key performance metrics (e.g., RPC%, PTP%, liquidation curves, roll rates) and deliver insights to leadership
- Ensure all strategies adhere to regulatory and compliance standards (e.g., TCPA, FDCPA, CFPB guidance)
- Support digital transformation initiatives, including automation and vendor integrations

The Ideal Candidate will have:
- Experience with customer, risk and portfolio segmentation
- Experience building and driving credit risk and collections strategies
- Experience with A/B Testing
- Familiarity with the test-and-learn framework
- Experience with experimental design
- Experience with decision-trees
- Champion/challenger testing

Depth & Scope:
- Demonstrates governance, control and risk management behaviors in alignment with TD policies and practices
- Leads/participates in the identification, development and implementation of new initiatives, operating workflow, additional services/applications or operational efficiencies including potentially leading special project teams or cross functional work groups
- Assists with developing and enhancing credit risk assessment capabilities to identify and maintain good business opportunities with new and existing clients
- Performs detailed analysis and interprets information to make recommendations to Senior Management on critical strategies including non-standard and ad-hoc requests as determined by management
- Creates reports on the results of implemented strategies, using all appropriate quantitative methods and MIS, and makes recommendations to increase efficiencies and revenue while managing credit risk and produce those reports on a regular basis
- Effectively works cross-functionally with teams outside of risk
- Works with Internal Audit / External Regulators, to ensure that documentation for all work processes is complete and up-to-date
- Ensures sound credit control by taking a pro-active approach to risk management within the risk guidelines of the Bank
- Ensures the timely communication of issues that are relevant to the team and encourages a good working relationship with other internal and external groups

Education & Experience:
- Bachelor's degree required; Graduate degree preferred
- 5+ years' experience required
- Proficient PC skills including a strong competency in MS Excel and PowerPoint, and a variety of PC-based analytical and reporting software packages
- Experience with the use of Relational Databases and the process of Extract Transform Load (ETL) using common languages such as SQL or SAS
- Familiar with various analytical or reporting tools, such as SAS, R, Matlab Tableau, etc.
- Strong analytical and problem solving skills are required to interpret data and draw conclusions
- Experience in data modeling and risk management either from a business administration, statistical, mathematical, scientific or financial background
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Experienced in developing and presenting recommendations to Senior Management

- Bachelor’s degree in STEM (e.g., Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, Economics)

- Familiarity with digital outreach channels (SMS, email, AI-driven engagement)

Job Description:
This role provides manager-level finance leadership for Corporate risk management financial reporting, governance, planning and forecasting, executive narrative, and cross-functional issue resolution. The Finance Manager owns outcomes within the assigned portfolio, exercises sound judgement to resolve complex issues, and makes timely, risk-informed decisions with appropriate escalation. The role proactively engages stakeholders across Finance, Treasury, business partners, control functions, central finance teams, and other groups to clarify requirements, challenge assumptions, understand inputs and downstream impacts, and drive improvements to processes, controls, analysis, and deliverables.

Job Summary
The Corporate Finance Manager – Risk Management integrates Corporate function Risk Management financial results, key drivers, significant items and variances, into clear management reporting and decision-support materials. The role takes end-to-end ownership of assigned outcomes, applies critical thinking and sound judgement to complex or ambiguous issues, and recommends or implements practical solutions. As a trusted finance partner, the Finance Manager constructively challenges inputs and assumptions, anticipates risks and opportunities, makes decisions within delegated authority, and continuously improves reporting, controls, stakeholder alignment, and ways of working. Success requires agility, accountability, and readiness to adapt priorities and approaches as business needs evolve.

Key Accountabilities
- Stakeholder relationship and outcome ownership: Own relationships and outcomes across Finance, business partners, control functions, central finance teams, and other stakeholders. Proactively clarify requirements, establish accountabilities and timelines, challenge assumptions constructively, and build the subject-matter knowledge needed to assess inputs, resolve gaps, and explain downstream impacts.
- Reporting, analysis, and insight: Lead financial reporting, variance and driver analysis, executive-ready narrative, and management reporting outputs. Apply critical thinking to distinguish underlying business drivers, draw clear conclusions, and deliver recommendations that support timely management decisions.
- Planning, forecasting, and allocations: Own assigned planning, forecasting, and methodology workstreams from definition through execution and follow-up. Evaluate assumptions, assess financial and operational impacts, make recommendations, and drive alignment and decisions with partner teams.
- Problem solving and decision making: Diagnose and resolve complex cross-functional issues involving treasury and liquidity impacts, stress testing, data quality, data lineage, reporting consistency, and close-cycle execution. Consider multiple variables, balance speed, accuracy, risk, and business impact, make decisions within delegated authority, and escalate selectively with clear options and recommendations.
- Controls, governance, and judgement: Apply a risk-based control mindset and sound professional judgement across reporting, planning, allocations, close-cycle execution, governance activities, and sensitive financial information. Identify emerging risks, challenge ineffective practices, and take timely action to strengthen control design and execution.
- Process improvement and change leadership: Challenge established ways of working and lead sustainable improvements that simplify processes, strengthen controls, reduce manual effort and noise, improve visibility, and enhance recurring deliverables. Translate identified opportunities into clear actions, decisions, and measurable outcomes, and adapt implementation plans as priorities or constraints change.
- Team leadership and constructive challenge: Set clear expectations, encourage respectful challenge and critical thinking, coach peers and analysts through complex work, and build capability through knowledge sharing and cross-training. Foster a collaborative culture focused on ownership, quality, inclusion, agility, accountability, and timely decisions and escalation.

Breadth & Depth
- Manager-level role with broad Corporate Segment impact and end-to-end accountability across finanial reporting, planning and forecasting, executive communications, process improvement, and partner engagement.
- Owns business outcomes—not only task completion—by integrating financial analysis, reporting challenge, recommendations, stakeholder alignment, risk considerations, and decision support within the assigned scope.
- Solves complex and ambiguous problems involving multiple variables and stakeholders; evaluates alternatives, makes risk-informed decisions, implements solutions, and escalates where authority, materiality, or risk requires it.
- Constructively challenges assumptions, established practices, and proposed solutions; communicates complex results, risks, issues, and recommendations in clear business language; and influences alignment and action with increasingly senior stakeholders.
- Operates with significant autonomy and sound judgement, adjusts priorities and approaches as business needs change, leads process and performance improvements, and guides analysts or specialists supporting related deliverables; generally reports to a Senior Manager or above.

Experience and Education
- Undergraduate degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related discipline.
- 7+ years of relevant finance experience, including management reporting, financial analysis, planning and forecasting, allocation support, treasury or liquidity reporting, stress testing, governance, controls, or close-cycle execution.
- Accounting designation preferred.
- Experience with executive reporting and commentary, allocation methodologies, earnings drivers, balance sheet or economic impacts, data quality, and cross-functional issue resolution is an asset.
- Demonstrated capability in ownership, complex problem solving, independent decision making, professional judgement, constructive challenge, and critical thinking. Strong communication, stakeholder-management, and influence skills are required, together with the agility and change readiness to improve processes, adapt to evolving priorities, and translate partner deliverables into clear finance impacts and actions.

Job Description:
Preferred Qualifications:

The Compliance Transformation team is focused on strengthening how TDS Compliance delivers against its most critical regulatory, remediation, technology, and control priorities. The team provides the structure, governance, and execution discipline needed to move complex initiatives from strategy to implementation, ensuring commitments are clearly defined, risks are actively managed, progress is transparent, and outcomes are aligned to regulatory expectations and business needs.

This Director, Compliance Transformation Program Manager plays a central part in that mandate by serving as the program management and execution lead for TDS Compliance’s transformation portfolio. It helps connect Compliance strategy to delivery by maintaining an integrated view of priorities, tracking remediation commitments, coordinating technology investment planning, challenging project owners on execution readiness, and producing senior-level reporting. In practice, the role ensures that high-priority initiatives are not managed in silos, but are coordinated, measurable, and delivered with the right level of accountability, transparency, and control focus.

- Lead program management for TDS Compliance initiatives, ensuring strong governance, disciplined execution, and timely delivery of strategic, regulatory, remediation, and control-related priorities.

This role will be responsible for overseeing the execution high priority and high visibility initiatives for TDS Compliance such as the DPA / DOJ Remediation, Market Conduct Remediation program, Control Enhancement Program, Compliance Evolution / Road to Strong initiative, etc.

Depth & Scope:
- Contribute to the program management function for TDS Compliance initiatives, ensuring strong governance, disciplined execution, and timely delivery of strategic, regulatory, remediation, and control-related priorities.
- Assist in maintaining an integrated portfolio view of remediation commitments, including regulatory, audit, self-identified, and management-driven initiatives, to support oversight and senior management reporting.
- Assist in overseeing remediation execution, including milestone tracking, dependency management, risk and issue identification, escalation, and support for resolving blockers or scope changes.

Job Description:
Preferred Qualifications:

DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW
The TD Securities Business Controls team is a first line of defense function responsible for providing risk and compliance advice, oversight, and effective challenge. The team helps business partners identify, assess, manage, monitor, and evidence risks across day-to-day activities, operations, products, services, payment capabilities, and change initiatives, while operating within risk appetite and meeting regulatory, policy, standard, and payment market infrastructure requirements.

Team members require strong first line governance and controls expertise, sound business judgment, and sufficient knowledge of transaction banking to assess whether the business is meeting internal and external expectations.

JOB DESCRIPTION
Reporting to the Managing Director, Business Controls, the Director supports the Transaction Banking Value Creation Plan (VCP) transformation and global Change Governance and serves as a trusted first line risk advisor to Transaction Banking stakeholders across TD Securities. The role provides coordinated risk guidance and challenge across payment products, rails, processing flows, platforms, operations, technology, clearing and settlement, and related payment market infrastructure obligations.

The Director acts as a central Governance and Controls relationship lead, connecting the business with specialist first line teams and second line risk partners. The role supports timely delivery of change by identifying the appropriate risk pathway, clarifying control and evidence expectations, escalating emerging risks, and ensuring decisions are transparent and well supported.
The position will be embedded with business and product leaders, Operations, Technology, Change Delivery teams, Compliance, Legal, Audit, Operational Risk, and other risk and control partners. Success requires strategic thinking, strong relationship management, practical risk judgment, and the ability to improve governance processes, controls, reporting, and tools.

JOB ACCOUNTABILITIES
• Serve as a senior trusted first line risk advisor to Transaction Banking leaders, providing practical governance, risk, and control guidance aligned with business strategy and risk appetite.
• Provide an integrated view of risk across payment products, rails, platforms, processing flows, operations, technology, clearing and settlement, and payment market infrastructure dependencies.
• Lead first line governance and effective challenge for payment-related change, including New Business and Product Approval, Change Risk Assessments, implementation readiness, post-implementation validation, transition to business-as-usual control ownership, and key delivery decisions.
• Coordinate engagement across the business, Product, Operations, Technology, Change Delivery, Compliance, Legal, Audit, Operational Risk, specialist first line teams, and second line partners based on risk and materiality.
• Provide oversight and challenge of payment processes, controls, risk assessments, evidence, and reporting
• Support first line risk owners in interpreting, implementing, monitoring, and evidencing governance requirements
• Review and challenge the completeness and adequacy of business assessments, control evidence, attestations, remediation plans, risk acceptances, and regulatory or industry-driven change initiatives.
• Monitor emerging risks, incidents, control gaps, issues, and remediation activities, escalating material concerns and systemic themes to business leadership and governance forums
• Maintain awareness of relevant regulatory, policy, industry, payment rail, and payment market infrastructure requirements and assess their implications for the business.
• Deliver clear, decision-useful reporting on aggregate risk, key indicators, control themes, incidents, issues, remediation status, and matters requiring management attention or decision.
• Partner with the business to prepare for control testing, audits, regulatory reviews, industry attestations, and other governance activities, ensuring risks and remediation plans are appropriately managed and evidenced.
• Strengthen risk culture and accountability by promoting constructive challenge, transparency, timely escalation, and evidence-based decision-making.
• Drive continuous improvement of the Change Governance framework, and first line interaction model while maintaining clear accountability across business and risk functions.
• Influence senior stakeholders by connecting client outcomes, business strategy, delivery priorities, operational resilience, regulatory expectations, and risk appetite.
• Lead, coach, and develop Governance and Controls colleagues, building transaction banking and risk capabilities within an inclusive, collaborative, high-performing team.

• 12-15+ years of experience in financial services, with significant experience in governance, business controls, risk management, regulatory compliance, transformation, or complex program delivery
• Demonstrated experience in Transaction Banking, Treasury and Trade solutions, payments, liquidity, cash management, client channels, platform and data services, and related operational and regulatory risks.
• Strong understanding of first line governance and controls responsibilities, effective challenge, and the respective accountabilities of the business, specialist functions, and independent second line oversight.
• Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide, multi-jurisdictional transformation programs, integrations, turnarounds, or control remediation initiatives in a highly regulated environment.
• Experience overseeing change risk, control design and effectiveness, implementation readiness, operational resilience, incidents, issues, remediation, attestations, and supporting evidence.
• Working knowledge of the regulatory, risk, policy, and industry landscape applicable to wholesale banking and transaction banking.  Payments experience is a plus.
• Proven ability to lead change, manage competing priorities, and deliver outcomes in a complex, global, and matrixed environment.
• Excellent judgment, with the confidence to challenge constructively, escalate material concerns, and support balanced, risk-based decisions.
• Strong relationship management, influencing, and communication skills, including the ability to translate complex payment and risk topics for executive audiences.
• Proven people leadership, coaching, and talent development skills, with experience building inclusive and collaborative teams.
• Strategic thinking, strong problem-solving skills; experience with large-scale technology delivery, agile ways of working, Jira, or Confluence is an asset.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

• Graduate degree a plus

Job Description:
Department Overview:

Our Finance team, called COO Finance, supports Transformation, Enablement and Customer Experience, which includes several innovative and customer focused business units such as DSIP (Digital Strategy, Innovation and Payments), SCOE (Strategy, Change and Operational Excellence), AI2 (Analytics, Insights & Artificial Intelligence), Marketing, and Enterprise Real Estate. The COO Finance team is comprised of energetic individuals committed to creating a high-quality finance support function delivering valuable insights and analysis.
The Finance Business Partner teams deliver strategic advice to partners within the Bank, provide effective controls, build plans and forecasts and financial reporting. The DSIP Finance team mandate includes:
- Performance Measurement & Analysis

- Planning & Forecasting

- Initiative Decision Support

- Value added analysis, advice, and guidance to business partners

We are currently looking to expand our DSIP Finance team.

Job Accountabilities:

The successful candidate for this position will report to the Senior Manager, DSIP and SCOE Finance. Their objective is to provide financial and business analysis and support the DSIP team. The Finance Manager must be a driver with strong leadership / communication skills and have experience in leading and delivering value-added business analysis, advice, and guidance. Candidates must be committed to professionalism, highly organized, able to see the big picture while paying attention to small details.

Key accountabilities for this position include:
- Serving as a Finance subject matter expert, while demonstrating a holistic viewpoint, on key components of DSIP Business and major DSIP initiatives. This will include frequent interaction with the business leaders

- Working with their business partners to build value proposition templates for major DSIP initiatives, and integrating them into mechanisms to track program spend

- Working with their business partners to build these initiatives into the annual financial plan and quarterly forecasts for their portfolio

- Being a leader in forecasting & planning by further building process excellence and leveraging partners to provide value add to the business

- Liaise with senior management and decision support team during the planning process to ensure initiatives are effectively incorporated into the business Annual Plan

- Conducting analysis of forecast results and broader trends to provide a reasonable view of the future of the business with advice to improve decision making

- Providing insightful and relevant commentary to Senior Management on business results, forecast and Plan

- Developing of monthly and quarterly operating result packages. Conduct progressive analysis on monthly results and provide value add advice, and guidance

- Being responsible to identify financial opportunities, conduct the necessary analysis to develop options and offer well supported recommendations to senior management.  This includes strong written and in-person presentation skills

- Proactively identifying issues and recommend actions to senior management

- Provide leadership and support to the DSIP Finance team, fostering a positive and rewarding work environment

- Working with senior management and lead in the development / implementation of new financial models, methodologies to support the business in understanding the financial impact of their decisions

- Use internal network to continually build specialized expertise to maximize customer satisfaction

- Support internal partners with ongoing projects and develop a clear understanding of how changes will affect a customer’s business

Job Description:
Department Overview.

The Franchise Banking Group is a dynamic team responsible for delivering competitive products and services to franchisee customers of TDBFG.  The Franchise Banking Group reports into the Commercial Advisory Service team within TD Business Banking and is responsible for growing the Bank's Franchise Banking portfolio with high-quality franchise systems. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Credit & Business Initiatives, Franchise Banking, the credit analyst has the responsibility to ensure that credit quality of the overall franchise portfolio at TD remains within TD's risk appetite.
The Analyst, Franchise Banking supports the Bank’s franchise programs with franchisors that are considered large commercial or junior corporate clients, spanning all industry sectors with the portfolio of franchise customers domiciled in both Small Business and Commercial segments. The position reports to the Senior Manager, Credit & Business Initiatives, Franchise Banking.

The Analyst is responsible for:
- Completing both new and annual program credit reviews, structuring programs to reflect Bank lending requirements (both Small Business and Commercial), risk appetite, and customer and franchisor needs.
- Monitoring and analyzing portfolio and franchise-system performance using Power BI dashboards and management reporting to identify emerging risks, negative trends, exceptions, concentrations, and opportunities, and providing decision-ready insights and recommendations to management.
- Maintaining the franchise database, Power BI dashboards, and recurring management reporting, including performing data validation, reconciliation, and quality-control activities to ensure information is accurate, complete, and reliable.
- Developing and enhancing Excel-based tools, models, macros, and other automated solutions to improve the efficiency and accuracy of credit analysis, portfolio monitoring, and reporting, while maintaining appropriate procedures and controls.
- Working with franchisors, franchisees, branches, and internal partners to resolve inquiries, address issues, and deliver timely, consistent service and reporting.
- Participating in franchisor visits and assisting the Origination Team in cross selling the full range of products and services to existing and new franchisors.
- Supporting the submission and implementation of new policies and guidelines within the Franchise Banking Group.

Job Requirements

- Knowledge and experience in Commercial Credit, ideally as an Analyst or Account Manager; Small Business Banking credit experience would be an asset.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data-management skills, with close attention to detail and the ability to translate complex information and large datasets into meaningful business and risk insights.
- Highly motivated, organized, and results-oriented self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.
- Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including strong credit writing and the ability to present complex analysis and recommendations clearly and concisely.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, pivot tables and macros/VBA, together with proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint and Word.
- Familiarity with Power BI dashboards and reporting would be viewed as an asset.

jobs.title: Senior Group Manager, Finance Governance & Controls (Capital Markets)
jobs.description:
Work Location:
Toronto, Ontario, Canada
Hours:
37.5
Line of Business:
Finance
Pay Details:
$115,600 - $163,200 CAD
TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description:
Department Overview
The Finance Governance & Controls (G&C) Team within the Controller & Chief Accountant's Department supports in fulfilling controllership and oversight and is responsible for governing, monitoring, and testing over risk and compliance policies for Finance. Finance G&C enables and supports Finance partners to identify, understand, manage, and mitigate risks in alignment with internal and regulatory expectations. We deliver risk and control testing, training, insights, and reporting to strengthen Finance's control environment and support high‑quality financial reporting.

Job Details
As a Senior Group Manager, you will be responsible for providing strategic guidance and oversight.  You will develop partnerships with cross-segment teams within Finance and across the Bank to provide expert advice on risk policies and control frameworks, identifying opportunities to improve processes and controls, and overseeing the implementation of changes. This role specifically supports the TD Securities Finance teams.
In this role you will:

Oversee Enterprise Risk Programs: Review, challenge and test adherence across Finance G&C programs (e.g., Financial Reporting Controls, RCSA, Regulatory Compliance Management, EUC Governance, Model Risk support, etc.). This would include managing deliverables and timelines with Finance partners, assessing evidence, documenting results, working with second-line Risk partners and ensuring quality of deliverables is in line with audit standards.
Identify Gaps & Recommend Actionable Remediation: Identify control design or operating effectiveness gaps across various areas of Finance. Provide clear, actionable recommendations to Finance partners. Review and challenge issues and operational risk events, support root‑cause discussions.
Validate Remediation Effectiveness: Perform and/or review validation testing to confirm remediation has been implemented and sustained. Prepare and/or review closure documentation that is complete, accurate, and audit‑ready.
Operate Across Multiple Programs with Agility: Shift smoothly between quarter end, testing cycles, risk reporting deadlines, and methodologies. Reprioritize, as needed to support Finance reporting timelines while applying consistent standards.
Clear & Practical Partner Support: Communicate expectations and findings in simple terms. Support Finance partners’ readiness, remediation clarity, and maintain strong cross‑team relationships.
Conduct Process Walkthroughs & Risk Assessments: Perform in-depth process walkthroughs and risk assessments with Finance partners to understand end‑to‑end processes, validate control points, and identify potential design or operating risks early in the cycle.
Reporting & Documentation: Prepare and/or review summaries, issue logs, and inputs for dashboards. Maintain complete, accurate, well‑organized documentation.
Subject matter expert on financial reporting controls: providing timely advice to senior management, business partners and stakeholders on complex financial reporting risks and controls, including preparing assessments on risks and controls and any gaps requiring remediation
Build for the future: Provide people leadership. Develop, coach, and train a team of professionals to accomplish positive outcomes and strengthen financial controls
Job Requirements
- Professional accounting designation (CPA, CA/CPA)

- University degree in business or other relevant fields

- 10+ years of experience in an accounting/finance/audit role with internal controls or financial controls experience

- Strong knowledge and experience with capital markets (products, structure, processes) and financial services experience is required

- Public accounting firm experience would be considered a strong asset

Job Description:
The Advisory and Contract Execution Team is an integral part of TD Securities.   The group provides best-of-class service to business partners in TD Bank Financial Group (the Bank) through negotiation and execution of agreements that govern capital markets trading products. The team is committed to providing a seamless client experience while managing the Bank’s risk.

The position will be responsible for providing best-of-class service to clients of TD Securities and internal business partners by preparing and negotiating legal documentation with global counterparties for trading products such as cash prime brokerage and equity derivatives, (i.e. Prime Brokerage Agreements, Term Commitment Agreements, ISDA Master Agreements, Credit Support Annexes, Account Control Agreements, Custody Agreements). The position must ensure that the Bank is sufficiently protected from legal, risk, and operational perspectives in all such trading documents and other legal documentation between the Bank and its counterparties.  The position will be required to build and maintain strong relationships with all stakeholders across the Bank and be available to service the deal flow with tight deadlines from global desks.

The Associate – Global Markets Documentation is responsible for providing best-of-class service to clients of TD Securities and internal business partners by preparing and negotiating legal documentation with global counterparties for trading products such as derivatives, foreign exchange and commodity products, i.e. ISDA Master Agreements, physical commodity agreements, and related credit support documentation.

Key Responsibilities:
- Assist with negotiations of Prime Brokerage Agreements, Term Commitment Agreements, ISDA Master Agreements, CSAs, Account Control Agreements and Custody Agreements with a variety of counterparties, including hedge funds and registered funds.

- Participate in internal calls with senior credit officers and front office contacts, as well as calls with clients and external legal counsel, to discuss issues that arise during negotiations of trading agreements and/or prime brokerage related documents.

- Liaise and coordinate with internal stakeholders, such as Credit, Business, Tax, Legal, Operations and Collateral Management, during the documentation process.

- Provide timely updates to the Business on the status of negotiations, whether via weekly calls or through the team's internal document tracking system.

- Support internal initiatives related to documentation, process automation, and regulatory compliance.

Depth & Scope:
- Negotiates a robust portfolio of capital markets regulatory agreements globally, ensuring regulatory compliance across specific trading products and jurisdictions, while aligning with internal risk, legal, regulatory and governance frameworks and ensuring accelerated time to market

- Reviews, drafts, and finalizes capital markets regulatory agreements across a range of trading products, ensuring alignment with internal standards and regulatory requirements

- Communicates capital markets regulatory requirements to business lines, clients and their legal counsel in an efficient, business-friendly manner

- Participates in client meetings and calls to provide regulatory advisory and rule interpretation, leveraging understanding of global derivatives regulations including US Dodd-Frank, EMIR, UK, Canadian, and Singapore frameworks

- Works with the trading desks to understand client needs and track and prioritize high value relationships

- Understands the current state of legislation, regulation, and guidance with respect to OTC derivative transactions globally including Canada, the US, the EU, the UK, Singapore, and other relevant jurisdictions

- Prepares and thoroughly reviews the necessary capital markets agreement requirements and disclosures to ensure TD Securities' regulatory obligations are met

- Participates in TD Securities-wide regulatory implementation efforts for new rules and initiatives, ensuring timely and accurate execution across jurisdictions

- Acts as a key point of contact for Front Office, Legal, Compliance, Credit, on regulatory documentation matters

- Reviews and analyzes TD Securities’ new and existing client base to ensure regulatory compliance daily

- Utilizes technology to track and monitor workflow, maintaining and updating databases with required information

- Produces reports and status updates as required

- Escalates issues proactively and in a timely manner

- Provides timely support across multiple time zones including North America, Europe, and Asia

Education & Experience:
- Law degree is required

- 1+ years of solid legal, trading documentation, capital markets, origination or related experience

Preferred Qualifications:
- New York Bar Admission

- 1+ years of experience (either at a law firm or a dealer)

- North American prime brokerage negotiation experience, together with experience negotiating term commitment agreements and custody agreements is a plus, but not a requirement.

- Experience negotiating ISDA Master Agreements, Credit Support Annexes and Account Control Agreements with hedge funds and registered funds is a plus, but not a requirement.

- The candidate for this position will enjoy working on legal trading documentation, be able to effectively apply legal and sound risk management principles and display good drafting ability.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, good PC skills and the ability to multi-task and meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced trading environment are requirements.

- Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills are essential.

- Ability to work under tight deadlines and flexibility to support global time zones as required.
